text:
olivia: Heads up — Ephemeral Debug Access (EDA) for Private deployments is GA starting today :rocket: This provides auditable, time-limited support sessions that customers can approve from their console. No keys are shared and every session is cryptographically attested. Docs + rollout below.

samir: big win for support ops. How does customer approval look?

olivia: customers get an in-console consent modal with session scope (read-only / read-write), duration (max 2h), and a cryptographic session token that is only valid for that window. All session activity is logged locally and included in the attestation package.

dario: rollout plan: pilot customers today, staggered to early access in 72h, full GA across Private clusters in 10 days. We'll enable EDA in disabled-by-default mode; customers must opt in per-cluster.

legal-bot: [NOTE] Legal reviewed the session attestation schema and approved for SOC/ISO evidence. Customers still responsible for explicit consent capture for regulated users.

samir: can customers require MFA or additional approvers before a session starts?

olivia: yes — console supports multi-approver policy and can require an Azure AD / Okta MFA check before a session token is minted. Policy is per-tenant.

support-bot: Support playbook: for EDA requests, open ticket with label "lab:eda-request". The ticket must include cluster id, requested scope, and approver email. Auto-task will generate the session request link.

kate-support: we'll run a 45-min enablement for support on Thursday 11:00 PT. recommend engineers join so we can triage live.

olivia: security details: sessions are brokered via an ephemeral proxy running inside the customer's VPC; proxy issues short-lived certs, logs are written to a locally mounted encrypted store, and attestations are signed by the customer's key or by Redwood's attestation key (customer selectable).

dario: config example for private-config.yaml: 
```yaml
ephemeral_debug_access:
  enabled: false  # default false for GA
  max_duration_minutes: 120
  require_multi_approver: true
  approver_count: 2
  session_logging:
    enabled: true
    retention_days: 90
  attestation:
    signer: customer_key  # options: customer_key | redwood_attest | none
```

samir: any perf impacts?

olivia: negligible — session proxy runs as a separate pod and uses streaming only during the session. Storage usage depends on log verbosity; with default audit-level logging estimate ~1-3% additional disk.

deploy-bot: [RELEASE] ephemeral-debug-access v1.0 deployed to canary Private clusters at 3261012390.

samir: edge cases: if a customer has network egress disabled, the session broker still works because all components run inside the VPC; remote support will ask for a console-signed bundle if they need Redwood to review logs off-network.

olivia: compliance note: EDA attestation artifacts are compatible with audit workflows for EU and US customers. For high-regulated customers we recommend turning on customer_key signing and multi-approver.

support-bot: Support: include session transcript and attestation hash in the ticket for post-incident review. Use label "lab:eda-audit" for any followups.

olivia: docs: https://redwood.internal/docs/private/ephemeral-debug-access (internal) — contains screenshots, API for session requests, and attestation verification steps.

kate-support: FYI to sales/AMs: we have a customer-facing one-pager and a compliance checklist; ping me for copies.

olivia: thanks all 1 monitoring metrics for first 72h: session-request-latency, session-duration, attestation-verification-failures. I'll post a short summary daily. :eyes:
